title: TeachBack: Learning to Teach via Bidirectional Preference Optimization for On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: TeachBack replaces standard on-policy self-distillation where the Teacher has static privileged access to the solution with a bidirectional preference-learning framework that shapes the Teacher's generation via reference-length control and prompt variation. It requires generating paired privileged and non-privileged trajectories at each rollout refresh and optimizing a pairwise preference objective, which increases training compute and implementation complexity compared to standard OPSD. The method can fail if the privileged Teacher trajectories, despite accuracy, omit the exploration and self-correction behaviors necessary for the Student to learn robust problem-solving without privileged information.
rationale: While the method targets distillation—a relevant area for constrained infrastructure—the requirement for on-policy bi-directional preference optimization with paired trajectory generation and custom reward modeling exceeds the limited compute and implementation budget of a small team without clusters.
